editorial:
Imagine having to face the hardest part of life when you are still just a kid. You follow a young boy named Yu and his father as they deal with his mother's serious illness. The vibe is very quiet and emotional, focusing more on feelings and images than on long speeches. It feels like a dream where small details tell you everything about how the family is hurting. You get to see the world through Yu's eyes, which makes the sadness feel more real because he is trying to understand something that adults usually keep secret.

What really works here is how the film uses visuals to show grief instead of just telling you about it. The acting feels natural and honest, though the slow pace might feel a bit long for some of you. If you enjoy stories that make you think and feel deeply, you will love this. Since it is a short film, it is best to watch it on a high-quality screen to catch all the artistic details.
endingExplained: The movie ends with Yu coming to terms with the fact that his mother cannot be saved. Through a series of poetic images, you see him move from fear to a quiet kind of acceptance. The final scenes show that while the pain of loss stays, the love between the father and son helps them move forward. It wraps up by showing that life continues even after a great loss, leaving you with a feeling of peace.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves heartfelt stories about family and healing.
